therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Pediatric and adult patients with autoimmune diseases of blood cells including ALPS, Evans syndrome, ITP, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, autoimmune neutropenia, autoimmune pancytopenia, SLE, IBD, and rheumatoid arthritis
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Number of participants with Grade 3 and 4 toxicities of administration of oral sirolimus at 6 months

results.effect_size: 1 out of 30 participants experienced Grade 3 or 4 toxicity
results.target_engagement_evidence: Mean sirolimus trough level 8.5 ng/mL (95% CI: 2.9–20) within first 5 days, within target range of 5–15 ng/mL
biomarker_changes: Mean sirolimus trough level 8.5 ng/mL (95% CI: 2.9–20 ng/mL) within first 5 days of starting sirolimus
subgroup_findings: ALPS patients (n=12): 11 CR, 1 PR, 0 NR, 0 PD for autoimmune disease response
Multilineage cytopenias patients (n=12): 7 CR, 1 PR, 2 NR, 2 PD for autoimmune disease response
Single-lineage autoimmune cytopenias patients (n=6): 1 CR, 2 PR, 3 NR, 0 PD for autoimmune disease response
ALPS patients lymphoproliferation response: 11 CR, 1 PR, 0 NR, 0 PD, 0 N/A
Multilineage cytopenias lymphoproliferation response: 3 CR, 0 PR, 1 NR, 1 PD, 7 N/A
Single-lineage autoimmune cytopenias lymphoproliferation response: 1 CR, 0 PR, 0 NR, 0 PD, 5 N/A
safety_signals: 1 serious adverse event of vasculitis reported in the sirolimus treatment group (1/30)
Only 1 participant experienced Grade 3 or 4 toxicity overall

dose_info.dose: Loading dose 3 mg/m2, then 2.5 mg/m2 with adjustment to target trough 5–15 ng/mL
dose_info.dose_modifications: Dose adjusted based on serum trough levels measured by high-performance liquid chromatography
